abstract: We explore the association between financial literacy and income satisfaction through the framework of relative deprivation, focusing on four distinct groups characterized by gender (men versus women), race (whites versus blacks), employment status (working versus retired), and disability (non-disabled versus disabled). Utilizing nationally representative data of over six thousand participants, our ordered logistic regression analysis reveals that, even after accounting for personality traits and other demographic factors, the connection between financial literacy and income satisfaction is notably weaker among the relatively deprived segments of women, blacks, and disabled individuals which could be attributed to disparities in earning opportunities. Conversely, this relationship is more pronounced among retired individuals. Our study broadens the scope of relative deprivation theory, highlighting its relevance to well-being measures such as income satisfaction and underscores the disproportionate impact that differences in financial literacy can have on various groups due to their respective experiences of relative deprivation.
abstract_zh: 我们通过相对剥夺的框架探讨金融素养与收入满意度之间的关联，重点关注四个不同群体：性别（男性与女性）、种族（白人与黑人）、就业状态（在职与退休）以及残疾状况（非残疾与残疾）。利用超过六千名参与者的全国代表性数据，我们的有序逻辑回归分析显示，即使在考虑人格特质和其他人口统计因素后，金融素养与收入满意度之间的联系在相对被剥夺的女性、黑人和残疾群体中显著较弱，这可能归因于收入机会的差异。相反，这种关系在退休个体中更为显著。我们的研究拓宽了相对剥夺理论的适用范围，强调其与收入满意度等福祉指标的相关性，并突显了金融素养差异因各群体相对剥夺经历的不同而对不同群体产生的非对称影响。
title: Relative deprivation and financial literacy in times of economic uncertainty: exploring income satisfaction across demographic groups
title_zh: 经济不确定性时期的相对剥夺与金融素养：不同人口群体收入满意度的探究
